metaDescription: Five dual-action car polishers under $100 compared on orbit throw, pad size, speed range, watt claims and what a budget DA polisher can correct on paint.
expertTake: A car polisher under $100 should be a dual-action machine, never a rotary, and the WORKPRO 6-inch is the best overall because it lists a 9 amp motor, a 15 mm orbit and up to 5,000 rpm with a side handle and several pads. The AOBEN 6-inch is the gentle, cheapest entry with a short throw, the AOBEN 5-inch long-orbit corrects faster, and the X'GLOW is the short-throw 5-inch for tight panels. The Aiderar cordless is a bare tool for DeWalt battery owners. Skip this tier if you plan to remove deep scratches from a whole fleet of cars.
introParagraphs: A dual-action polisher spins its pad while also oscillating it, which spreads heat and friction across the paint so you cannot easily burn through the clear coat the way you can with a fixed-axis rotary buffer. That safety margin is why DA machines are the right choice for beginners and for anyone polishing their own car.

At a low price, the differences are in orbit size, speed control and the vibration you feel after twenty minutes. This guide explains each, how to read inflated watt claims and what a budget polisher can realistically correct. The quick picks are above, and the reviews below match each machine to a type of owner.

products.name: WORKPRO 6-Inch Dual Action Random Orbital Polisher, 9 Amp, 15 mm Orbit

specList.label: Handles
specList.value: Grip hood and auxiliary side handle

products.description:
The WORKPRO is the best buy because it lists a motor figure that makes sense, 9 amps, and an orbit size that does real correction. A 15 mm orbit, also called throw, is a medium-long stroke: it moves the pad farther per cycle than a 9 mm short-throw machine, so it cuts and corrects swirl marks faster while still being forgiving. A short-throw 9 mm machine is gentler but slower.

Six speed steps up to 5,000 rpm let you match pad speed to the job: low speeds for spreading wax and sealant, medium for polishing, and high for compound. A 6-inch pad covers more paint per pass than a 5-inch, which speeds up work on hoods and roofs. A grip hood and an auxiliary handle reduce fatigue, and the kit includes multiple pads.

Against the AOBEN 6-inch, the WORKPRO has a stated orbit and a stronger motor figure. Against the AOBEN 5-inch with a 16 mm throw, it is about equal in correction but with a bigger pad. Keep the pad flat on the paint, work in small sections and let the machine do the work, since pressing hard stalls the pad rotation and lets friction build. Prime the pad with a few small dots of polish and spread at low speed before raising it.
products.bestFor: Beginners and weekend detailers who want a balanced 6-inch DA with real correction ability.
pros: 15 mm orbit corrects swirls faster than short-throw machines
Auxiliary handle and grip hood reduce fatigue
cons: 6-inch pad is awkward on tight curves
Budget machine vibrates after long sessions

products.name: AOBEN 5-Inch Dual Action Polisher, 16 mm Long Orbit, 6 Speeds
products.description:
The AOBEN 5-inch has the longest orbit in the group at 16 mm, which is the specification that matters most for paint correction. A long throw spreads the cutting action over a wider arc, so a DA machine removes swirls and light scratches faster, closer to the performance of a rotary buffer but with the safety of a dual-action motion. On a budget machine, long throw is the best path to faster results.

Ignore the 1,600W claim. A 120V household circuit supplies at most about 1,800W at 15 amps, so a hand-held polisher claiming 1,600W is quoting a peak or a marketing figure, not what the motor delivers. The kit includes six foam pads and a wool disc, enough to cut, polish and finish, plus a side handle that fits on either side.

A 5-inch pad is easier to control on curved panels, mirrors and door edges, which makes the AOBEN the more precise tool for small areas. Against the WORKPRO, it has a slightly longer throw and a smaller pad. Expect more vibration from a long-throw machine, and use a lighter touch to avoid hopping. Work in a two-foot-square section with overlapping passes and light pressure.
products.bestFor: Detailers who want faster correction in a 5-inch pad for curves and tight areas.
pros: 16 mm long orbit corrects faster than 9 mm machines
Seven pads included in the kit
cons: Smaller pad is slower on large panels

products.name: X'GLOW 5-Inch Corded Dual Action Polisher, 900W, 9 mm Orbit, 6 Speeds

specList.label: Speed use
specList.value: Low for wax, medium for polish, high for compound

products.description:
The X'GLOW is the short-throw 5-inch machine, and it is a better choice than it may look. A 9 mm orbit is gentler than a 15 or 16 mm throw, which makes it easier to control, quieter in the hand and less likely to hop on a curve. It corrects more slowly, but a beginner who corrects slowly and safely beats one who fights a machine that hops.

The maker gives clear guidance on six speeds: low for waxing and finishing, medium for polishing and high for compound. That mapping is correct and worth following, since compound at low speed does little and wax at high speed flings off. A corded 900W motor avoids battery swaps, and the figure is credible, falling below the 1,800W ceiling of a household circuit.

Against the AOBEN 5-inch, the X'GLOW is a gentler, slower machine with a modest power claim. Against the AOBEN 6-inch, it shares the 9 mm throw but with a smaller pad. It is a good first polisher for anyone worried about damaging paint. Use light pressure and overlap each pass by about half. Wipe the residue off after each section so you can check your progress under good light.
products.bestFor: First-time polishers who want a gentle, controllable machine.
pros: 9 mm orbit is gentle and easy to control
Clear speed guidance for wax, polish and compound
cons: Corrects slowly compared with 15 mm machines

products.name: AOBEN 6-Inch Dual Action Car Polisher, 700W, 6 Speeds, 4 Pads

specList.label: Handles
specList.value: Side handle fits both sides, top handle

specList.label: Kit
specList.value: 3 foam discs and 1 synthetic wool disc

products.description:
The AOBEN 6-inch is the lowest-priced polisher here, and its 700W motor is the most modest. That lower power is not a flaw for a DA polisher: the cutting action comes from pad speed and orbit, and a smaller motor simply stalls sooner if you press too hard. A 6-inch pad covers more paint per pass, so it is quick on hoods and roofs.

It does not state an orbit size, which makes it harder to compare. Compared with the WORKPRO's 15 mm and the AOBEN 5-inch's 16 mm, assume it is a shorter throw and treat it as a gentle machine. Three foam discs and a synthetic wool disc come with the kit, along with a side handle that mounts on either side and a top handle.

It is a good machine for applying wax and sealant and for light polishing, but it will struggle with heavy compounding. The wool disc is meant for removing excess wax. For a first machine on a tight budget it is a safe, simple choice. Use light pressure and keep the pad moving. Replace the pad when the foam breaks down, since a worn pad glazes and stops cutting.
products.bestFor: Budget buyers who mainly polish lightly and apply wax and sealant.

products.name: Aiderar Cordless Car Buffer Polisher for DeWalt 20V MAX, Brushless, 15 mm Orbit
products.description:
The Aiderar is a bare tool for people who already own DeWalt 20V MAX batteries. It pairs a brushless motor with a 15 mm orbit and a five-speed dial, so it matches the WORKPRO's correction ability without a cord. A cordless polisher is genuinely useful for detailing: no cord to drag across clean paint, no outlet needed in the driveway.

The listing is clear that you must supply the battery and charger, and that it is made for DeWalt users. Compared with the corded polishers, it depends on battery capacity, and polishing is a steady, long draw, so use a 4 Ah pack or larger and keep a spare. A brushless motor wastes less energy, which helps run time. The listed 1,000W is a maker figure and should be treated cautiously.

Against the WORKPRO, the Aiderar costs about the same without batteries but gives you cordless freedom if you have them. If you do not own DeWalt batteries, the WORKPRO is the better buy. Check the pad's backing plate size and keep spare pads, and avoid leaving the battery on the tool between sessions. Keep the cord over your shoulder to avoid dragging it across paint.
products.bestFor: DeWalt 20V MAX owners who want a cordless detailing polisher.
pros: Cordless, so no cord drags on clean paint
Uses batteries you may already own
cons: Bare tool without battery or charger

buyingCriteria.explanation: Throw is how far the pad swings in each orbit. A 9 mm machine like the X'GLOW is gentle and slow, a 15 mm machine like the WORKPRO and Aiderar corrects faster and a 16 mm machine like the AOBEN 5-inch is fastest. Long throw is better for swirl marks, short for control. Beginners often prefer 9 mm. A common mistake is to tilt the pad on an edge, which concentrates heat, so keep it flat and avoid body lines and sharp creases.

buyingCriteria.criterion: Dual action is the safe choice
buyingCriteria.explanation: A dual-action machine spins and oscillates, which spreads heat and makes burn-through unlikely, while a rotary buffer spins on a fixed axis and can burn paint in seconds. All five picks here are dual action. Never use a rotary on a car unless you have trained. Many first-time buyers choose a 6-inch pad and then struggle on mirrors and door jambs, which is why a 5-inch machine is worth owning too.

A 120V, 15 amp circuit supplies about 1,800W maximum, so the AOBEN 5-inch's 1,600W claim is not credible for a hand-held tool. The WORKPRO's 9 amp, 1080W and X'GLOW's 900W are more realistic. Look for amps, which are easier to verify. Use painter's tape on trim and edges before polishing, since a pad catching a plastic edge can scuff it.

A 6-inch pad covers flat panels quickly, like the WORKPRO and AOBEN 6-inch. A 5-inch pad, like the AOBEN 5-inch and X'GLOW, reaches curves, mirrors and door jambs. Many detailers use both. Test your polish on a small hidden area first, since a very aggressive pad and compound can remove more paint than you want.

Low speeds spread wax and sealant, medium speeds polish and high speeds work compound. All picks have five or six steps. Check that the dial is smooth and that the speed holds under load. Clean the paint with a clay bar before polishing, because embedded grit will scratch under the pad.

Corded machines like the WORKPRO run indefinitely, while the Aiderar's battery limits sessions. Budget polishers vibrate, and a side handle reduces fatigue. A machine that is uncomfortable to hold leads to uneven polishing. Check the machine's balance by holding it at arm's length, since a nose-heavy polisher tires the wrist fast.

specDecoder.meaning: The width of the pad's oscillation, in millimeters. Long throw covers more area per cycle. Pad rotation is slower than spin rpm on a free-spinning DA, because the pad stalls when pressed to paint.
specDecoder.watchFor: The AOBEN 6-inch does not state it. Assume a short throw.

specDecoder.meaning: DA machines quote spin rpm or orbits per minute. The LDHTHOPI lists 2,800 to 5,800. A longer throw is not always better, since it makes the machine harder to control near edges.
specDecoder.watchFor: Check which unit is used before comparing.

specDecoder.meaning: Watts are volts times amps. A 9 amp motor at 120V draws about 1,080W. A 15 amp circuit is limited to about 1,800W, which is why larger watt claims are suspect.
specDecoder.watchFor: A claim above 1,800W is not credible on a household circuit.

specDecoder.meaning: Five and six inches are the common sizes. The backing plate must match the pad. Hook-and-loop pads must match the backing plate diameter for even wear.
specDecoder.watchFor: A 6-inch pad on a 5-inch plate leaves an unsupported edge.

specDecoder.meaning: A motor without brushes, more efficient and long-lived. Brushless motors also run quieter and cooler on long sessions.
specDecoder.watchFor: Only the Aiderar lists brushless here.

howToChoose.note: Start gentle and move up if you need more correction.

maintenance.why: Dried polish hardens pads and scratches paint. Unplug before changing pads.
A worn plate loses grip and vibrates. Wash pads with a mild cleaner.
A damaged cord is a hazard. Check the hook face for wear.
Polish dust overheats the motor. Wipe the body with a damp cloth.
Heat ages lithium cells. Store pads flat and dry.

faq.q: Is a DA polisher safe for beginners?
faq.a: Yes. The dual-action motion makes burn-through unlikely. Always wash and dry the car before polishing, and work in shade on a cool panel.

faq.q: How many passes do I need?
faq.a: Work in 2 by 2 foot sections with several overlapping passes. Wipe off residue with a clean microfiber towel and inspect under good light.
A cutting pad for compound, a polishing pad for polish and a soft pad for wax. Finish with a wax or sealant to protect the corrected paint.
Not usually. A DA removes light swirls and oxidation, not deep scratches.

faq.q: How do I stop slinging polish?
faq.a: Use a small amount, start at low speed and keep the pad flat.

faq.q: Do I need a cordless polisher?
faq.a: No. Corded is cheaper and never runs out.
